approach: Re-spec brief delivery on the spawn path in packages/cyberlegion only: the wake carries the instruction to read the brief and begin, replacing the content-free doorbell; the SessionStart hook's spawning->active brief-injection branch is retired as redundant. Mechanism already exists (MuxAdapter.submit/nudge via unit nudge --message) — this is a contract change plus a dead-path retirement, not new plumbing.

Touches mail/surface, unit/lifecycle, mail/doorbell. Expected to narrow frozen scenarios in mail/surface (first-hook-call injects the brief; later call does not re-inject) and unit/lifecycle (brief-by-file, typed launch command carries no brief text; first-turn doorbell block).

Clearance floor GRANTED LIVE by the owner before drafting — the owner was shown the frozen-scenario re-open and the ADR supersession and selected the option naming both. Recorded here per grant-then-record; the narrowing edits follow the spec gate, not this line.
Supersedes ADR-0027 (spawn delivers the first turn), which split payload-delivery from turn-delivery deliberately. The superseding ADR is in this CR, not a follow-up.
leash auto-none: owner is live in-session and both gates are cheap to ratify; emit a verdict and stop at each gate rather than self-assert over a Clearance floor.

Out of scope, filed as follow-ups at handoff: CR-B the cyberlegion-plugin lifecycle abstraction and its frameless-unroutable case; CR-C cyberfleet Operator adopting the seam plus its stale hook prose.

why: Cold sdd-spec-judge round 3 over the re-spec of spawn brief delivery: oracle/builder/architect all PASS, ALIGNED true, SCENARIOS_FAILING [], no blocker, no open markers. The wake now carries the instruction (read the brief at its file path and begin, naming the path rather than carrying the body); the SessionStart hook's brief-injection branch is retired, which removes the only reader of `spawning` and the only transition to `active`, so spawn registers `active` directly. Narrowing, not additive: `mail/surface` loses both brief-injection scenarios and `unit/lifecycle` rewrites the first-turn doorbell step plus the pre-registration status -> both features unfreeze and re-freeze at this gate under Clearance, granted live before drafting (seq 1) and re-affirmed at ratification. Three rounds: R1 short-circuited on a governance pre-flight miss (0 of 7 bars declared); R2 returned builder FAIL on a real discrimination defect — the replacement `mail/surface` scenario was a barred edge with no firing-direction companion, its Given pinning the brief file but not the peer's registry status, so under the only constructible fixture (`active`) the un-retired inject-inbox.ts:40 branch is inert and a partial implementer passed every Then; R3 verified the owner's chosen remedy (freeze the retirement with a legacy-`spawning` record scenario) kills that subject two independent ways and re-derived R2's fixes independently. `mail/doorbell` was in the intake estimate but is NOT touched — no scenario there references the spawn doorbell. check-spec-state OK; check-suite unavailable in-repo (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, npx-only engine), so suite form was judged by hand, not linted.

Second-pass spec gate, cold sdd-spec-judge round 6: oracle/builder/architect all PASS, ALIGNED true, SCENARIOS_FAILING [], no blocker. The first pass (seq 2) was ratified at 24 and 60 scenarios and then RE-OPENED, because the conformance work behind it had built both nodes' scenario maps BACKWARD — each existing scenario matched to a control-flow edge, making the map 1:1 by construction and structurally incapable of surfacing a coverage hole, the one thing it was added to do. A cold re-derivation (one blind agent per node, fed only the implementation and the node's What/Use Cases, never the .feature or the map) found 40 coverage holes and ~11 vacuous scenarios across two suites that both reported full coverage. The owner extended the Clearance grant live to close all 40 and to fix frozen scenarios in place; blast was raised medium -> high accordingly, since this re-judges two nodes end to end rather than a two-node delta. mail/surface went 24 -> 35 scenarios, unit/lifecycle 60 -> 87. Six rounds, five of them one migrating defect class: an absence assertion that could not fail. R1/R2 found refusals asserting the throw but not the absence of what the guard prevents, fixed at the named sites and recurring at new ones both times. R3's mechanical sweep closed every absent absence and introduced inert ones, then named the invariant that closed it — every absence Then must be loseable on its own Given, which means naming the wrong implementation and the concrete artifact it produces. R4 applied it to all 104 absence assertions. R5 caught an absence wearing positive syntax that five keyword-keyed sweeps had missed. R6 swept a third axis and the no-marker residual and found nothing. Findings by round: 4, 4, 4, 1, 1, 0. Three implementation defects the cold read surfaced are specified as they behave and filed as follow-ups, not fixed here, on the owner's call. All six deterministic checks green.
